FGF-23
FGF-23 is a hormone secreted in the bone that reduces phosphorus serum concentration by decreasing renal reabsorption and by
decreasing 1,25(OH)2D3 synthesis, which decreases intestinal phosphorus absorption (Ureña and De Brauwere, 2011). FGF-23
needs FGF receptors, and Klotho, a transmembrane protein, as a co-receptor in order to lower phosphorus concentrations (Bergwitz
and Jüppner, 2010; Lanske and Razzaque, 2014; Ureña and De Brauwere, 2011). Both PTH and 1,25(OH)2D3 can induce FGF-23
expression in the bone, and PTH can also regulate Klotho expression in the kidney (Lanske and Razzaque, 2014).
Hyperphosphatemia and its consequences
Hyperphosphatemia (serum phosphate >4.5 mg/dL) may be caused by three main mechanisms: decreased phosphorus renal excre-
tion, excessive phosphorus intake and a shift from intracellular to extracellular phosphorus. Signs and symptoms of hyperphospha-
temia are similar regardless of the cause (Leung and Crook, 2019).
